issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for Pneumatic.openValve: the problem statement UML declares openValve() with no parameters, but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares openValve(int duration). Additionally, the solution's implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) define openValve() with no parameters, which conflicts with the interface declaration. This inconsistency (UML vs. interface, and interface vs. implementations) will cause compilation errors and confuse students about the correct method signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic.openValve signature consistent across all artifacts. Option A (preferred to match UML): change the solution interface method to 'void openValve();' in src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java and remove the int parameter from all implementations (LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster). Option B: if a duration parameter is intended, update the problem statement UML to declare openValve(duration: int) and update the implementing classes to override openValve(int duration). Ensure the template, solution, and any tests use the same signature.
